message.content: {"verdict":"revise","score":0.62,"reasons":["Artifact is truncated and incomplete: it ends mid-section with \"Typical usable depth of discharge\" and contains missing substantial content (DoD, calendar life, temperature ranges, thermal management, safety incidents, recycling, supply chain, field deployments) for both chemistries.","Missing or inconsistent citations: the text references placeholders like [CATL; pv‑magazine; Notebookcheck] [refs 4,7,6] and lacks a complete bibliography with URLs for every fact or figure as required.","Li-ion details are largely summarized in the executive section but lack the comprehensive, itemized data requested (cell/pack energy density, costs, cycle life, calendar life, RTE, DoD, temperature range, safety, supply chain, recycling, products, deployments) with accompanying sources.","The document is not yet deployment-ready for decision-making: no dedicated conclusions section, no complete product/pricing data, no field deployment examples, and no complete residential-oriented analysis across both chemistries."] ,"guidance":"Revise by delivering a complete, citation-supported comparison suitable for residential decision-making. Specifically: 1) include a full, sectioned attributes table for both Na‑ion and Li‑ion covering: cell/pack energy density (Wh/kg and Wh/L), cost per kWh (manufacturing and installed/system), cycle life (cycles at the recommended DoD), calendar life (years), round‑trip efficiency (%), usable DoD (%), operating temperature range and thermal management needs, safety incidents/thermal runaway risk, material supply chain and scarcity (Li/Na, Co/Ni, etc.), recycling/end‑of‑life pathways, representative commercial products with specs and prices, and notable field deployments. 2) provide a transparent, dated bibliography with URLs for every fact/figure; cite primary sources (manufacturer datasheets, regulatory filings, independent reviews, market reports). 3) add a concise conclusions section with a clear recommendation (which chemistry is preferable today for typical residential use, under what conditions Na‑ion could become preferable). 4) ensure the document is complete (no truncated sentences), consistently formatted (markdown is fine), and explicitly addresses residential/home applications. 5) flag uncertainties and ranges with context (e.g., regulatory status, UL‑9540 listings, field data vs. lab claims). 6) remove or replace placeholder references with real citations and include a comprehensive bibliography section."}
